subject: Workplace Skills
title: Meeting Norms and Agreements
description: Learn Meeting Norms and Agreements in one minute.

hook.text: One team agreed: laptops closed, phones away, start on time. Within a month their meeting satisfaction doubled.

buildup.text: Norms are unwritten rules that shape group behavior. Explicit norms are more powerful than implicit ones.

discovery.text: Co-creating norms as a team generates buy-in. Imposed rules create resentment. Chosen rules create ownership.

twist.text: Norms only work if leaders follow them. A boss checking their phone while others have them away kills compliance.

climax.text: Facilitate a 15-minute session: 'What three meeting behaviors do we want as a team?' Post them visibly. Revisit monthly.

punchline.text: Co-create the norms. Leaders model first. Culture follows.

quiz.question: Why should meeting norms be co-created rather than imposed?
options: It takes less time than writing rules yourself
Co-created norms generate buy-in while imposed rules create resentment
Employees have more meeting experience than managers
